subject: Delegation letters & proof-of-integration flow for subprocessor attestations
thread_content:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: delegation letters + proof-of-integration flow for subprocessors

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review we need a short set of artifacts to complete our security sign-off:

- Delegation letters or contractual language that shows Redwood has delegated controls to named subprocessors (or confirmation there are none in scope).
- A simple proof-of-integration flow showing how data flows to each subprocessor (diagram or bullet list).
- KMS/residency statement for any services that hold customer keys.
- A compact SBOM or component roster for the inference runtime (stub OK if you can follow up with an SBOM delivery plan).

Can you send these by the end of next week (12 May)? We have a Trustwave SOC team doing an intake and they'd like to review before the contract is routed.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Procurement
HealthGrid

---

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: delegation letters + proof-of-integration flow for subprocessors

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a delegation letter template signed by Redwood for the subprocessors in scope, plus a short dataflow summary per provider and a KMS residency attestation. SBOM: we can provide a compact inventory now and a full SBOM delivery plan (target 30 days) if that works for you.

Deliverables we will attach/deliver by 12 May:
- Signed delegation_letter_HealthGrid_2027-05-12.pdf (templated, lists onshore/offshore residency)
- Redwood_Subprocessor_Roster_2027-05-12.csv (names, roles, countries, control class)
- kms-key-residency-attestation_jonas_2027-05-11.pdf (high level attestation from infra team)
- sbom-inventory_stub.txt (component list + follow-up schedule)

Process notes:
- For delegation letters we issue an internal sign-off and then DocuSign to you (link will be in the Drive folder).
- For any subprocessor that requires a deeper proof (e.g., on-prem partner), we can provide a scoped control mapping (SIG-lite) under NDA.

I'll loop in Ben and Jonas to confirm the KMS/residency language and SBOM stub.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

---

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: delegation letters + proof-of-integration flow for subprocessors

Ben / Jonas —

HealthGrid needs the artifacts below by EOD 12 May. Quick asks:
- Ben: can you export the current subprocessor roster CSV from the registry and flag any onshore-only vs global providers? Include contact and purpose.
- Jonas: please produce a one-page KMS attestation indicating where customer keys (if any) can be held, whether we hold wrapped keys in our environment, and a residency statement for any third-party KMS. Minimal language is fine; we'll review and I may edit for procurement.
- SBOM: Ben, a stub inventory (component names + versions) is OK for now. Add a short note with timeline to full SBOM delivery.

I'll assemble the delegation letter template and drop everything in the shared Drive + send the DocuSign envelope once signed. If either of you see any blocking compliance/regulatory constraints for HealthGrid (they process regulated health data), flag immediately.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 08:03 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Forwarding HealthGrid request.

Olga

---

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 May 2027 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: delegation letters + proof-of-integration flow for subprocessors

Thanks — I'm on it. Quick status:
- Subprocessor roster exported and attached as Redwood_Subprocessor_Roster_2027-05-12.csv (includes fields: name, purpose, country, data classification, contact).
- SBOM stub attached (sbom-inventory_stub.txt) — includes runtime libs and base container layers; security team to produce full SBOM within 30 days (JIRA SEC-2043).
- Flagged two providers with sensitive processing (kms-managed logging partner and on-prem model tuning vendor). I noted residency differences in the CSV.

I'll leave the KMS attestation to Jonas — once he drops his PDF I'll attach and we can finalize the delegation letter.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Subprocessor_Roster_2027-05-12.csv (CSV, 1.2KB), sbom-inventory_stub.txt (TXT, 3.4KB)

---

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 May 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: delegation letters + proof-of-integration flow for subprocessors

Attached: kms-key-residency-attestation_jonas_2027-05-11.pdf (attestation). Key points in the attestation:
- Redwood stores customer-wrapped keys when customers choose Redwood KMS integration; we do not extract plaintext keys.
- For cloud-managed keys where a third-party KMS is used, residency depends on the customer's region and is recorded on a per-customer basis.
- For HealthGrid we recommend onshore residency (US) and can confirm the key handle residency in the Doc our infra team will sign.

Also included a one-paragraph description of how key handles are referenced by our runtime; safe to share with procurement.

Jonas Weber
Infrastructure Security Lead
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stub: kms-key-residency-attestation_jonas_2027-05-11.pdf (PDF, 1.1KB)

Hi Liam / Procurement team —

Per our commitment, please find the initial evidence bundle attached and the shared folder below. If anything requires greater depth (SIG responses, SOC artifacts), we can escalate via NDA and provide a scoped bundle.
